enumeration.method: Independent inspection of all bold CMBX10 Theorem headings across the 50-page main-paper PDF finds exactly Theorems 1-7. Ordinary-font mentions, proof citations and other result labels are excluded. Theorem 4 has a type-B continuation on page 24. A supplement notice on physical page 43 links to a separate unopened document; references and main-paper figures continue to page 50.

checks: The independent inventory and final census pass separate validator calls; the inventory hash matches its prior source review and all original claim fields survive unchanged.

The title, four authors, arXiv v4 stamp of 1 October 2023, versioned URL, 50-page count and PDF digest agree with the inspected source. Physical page 43 corrects the outline’s off-by-one supplement location; no supplement body is embedded or used.

All seven complete theorem statements were visually checked on pages 12,15,18,23,24,26,27, including both hinge-policy branches, the exact regret divisor, all type-dependent approximation rates and every finite-sample growth/probability condition.

The longitudinal record, histories, potential-outcome context, two propensity functions and separate assumptions I-IV were checked on pages 5-7. The conditional-integrability formulas retain their distinct absolute-value scopes.

The source optimal policies, measurable score class, original and surrogate values, maximizing-score rules, regrets and eta maps were checked on pages 7-9. Extended maximizer conventions and the absence of attainment requirements in Definition 1 remain explicit.

Theorem 1 depends on sequential Fisher consistency and the source closedness/strict-concavity conventions. Theorem 3 gives a regret inequality and does not acquire the Fisher-consistency predicate merely because the following prose deduces consistency.

The generic surrogate definition does not inherit Condition 2. That condition is used only by Theorems 3-7; hinge loss and its reward condition are confined to Theorem 2, and the two derivative types are confined to Theorem 4.

Outcome bound A applies to Theorems 4-7; small-noise B to Theorems 4/5; literal strong-separation C to Theorems 6/7. The graph does not treat the source C as an equivalent version of B or repair its center from zero to one half.

Empirical value, fitted product classes and optimization error are resolved for Theorems 5-7. Theorem 5 uses the coordinatewise sup-norm condition (21); Theorem 6 uses logarithmic empirical-L2 condition (23); Theorem 7 retains its inline pair-class bracketing-number bound (24).

Theorem 7 does not inherit Opt_n<1/2 or rho_n<1 from Theorem 6. The general-class theorems do not inherit neural-network, wavelet, Assumption D, derivative-type or optimizer-convergence assumptions from examples or proofs.

Fourteen auxiliary passages and twenty-four source notes resolve effective domains, norm and probability conventions, known propensities, outcome positivity, common noise exponent and source inconsistencies. Independent graph checks cover 61 direct uses and 126 related-theorem connections, with matching source selectors and explanations for every interface.

source_notes: The census uses the pinned arXiv v4 preprint; identity with the final journal wording has not been established.
No separate supplement was opened. Its proof references remain references, and unresolved assumptions or claims are not repaired using material outside the main paper.

Source fidelity and dependency validation do not certify proof correctness. The literal positivity quantifier, treatment coding, strict-concavity diagonal, strong-separation center, later value display and entropy quantifier issues remain documented.
The source calls a bracket count bracketing entropy. Its actual N and log N conditions remain distinct, with the stated norms and exponents unchanged.

All source definitions and conditions retain their original labels, with natural-language source keywords and notation kept in the detailed passages. Standard ambient primitives are resolved separately without inventing additional theorem claims.

unresolved_source_references.note: The source quantifies pi_t(A_t|H_t)>C_pi at the realized action rather than explicitly for both possible actions. Read literally, a deterministic assignment can satisfy this realized-action statement, although positivity for identifying all regimes requires support for the counterfactual actions. The recorded assumption is not silently strengthened.

Potential covariates and outcomes are described verbally and are not fully indexed by intervention histories. Sequential ignorability names Y_t and O_(t+1), and its precise joint counterfactual scope is not expanded in the main text. The census retains the original formulation and the claimed identification relation.

The source requires conditional statements at every history, including possible null histories, without specifying versions. Its first-stage conditional bound has no absolute value, unlike the second-stage bound. The positive outcome convention helps with finiteness but does not resolve conditional-version choices.

unresolved_source_references.note: Adding a finite constant cannot make arbitrary integrable outcomes with unbounded negative support uniformly positive. Moreover, the source itself notes that shifting outcomes can change the hinge condition (13). Positive outcomes are retained as a model restriction where imposed, not declared irrelevant for surrogate policies.
H_2 is defined as (O_1,Y_1,O_2,A_1), while Theorem 2 writes h_2=(h_1,a_1,y_1,o_2). The ordering discrepancy is retained, with the conceptual history components identified separately.

The action space is {-1,1}, but the indicator policy formula produces {0,1}, and Theorem 4 gives htilde_n,2 an extra {0,1} factor even though H_2 already includes A_1. Neither coding nor the extra argument is silently changed.

unresolved_source_references.note: Remark 1 fixes optimal ties to +1, whereas the eta paragraph assigns -1 otherwise after the strict >1/2 case. Theorem 2 also uses set-valued surrogate rules yet writes a_1=dtilde_1(h_1) as a scalar equality. Set membership is not substituted for the printed equality.

The strict indicators yield no reward contribution when a score is zero. The following prose permits either action at zero, which need not match that formula for positive rewards. The original formula and tie claims are both preserved.

The source writes V_psi* through an extended-valued maximizer, then explicitly says Definition 1 does not require such maximizers to exist or be measurable. The corresponding supremum is recorded as the interpretation of the optimum; no attainment assumption is added to Fisher consistency.

The printed strict-concavity inequality quantifies all x,y in the effective domain without excluding x=y, making the literal inequality impossible at a repeated point. The original passage is saved, and the usual distinct-point restriction is not inserted into it.

The first branch is stated at h_1, but its failure conclusion uses capital H_1. The theorem does not specify how to choose a surrogate maximizer jointly across histories before stating all stagewise alternatives. The exact h_1/H_1 and scalar/set notation are retained.

The paper uses min(x-1,y-1,0), a figure caption max(x-1,y-1,0), and the Theorem 2 function min(x,y,1). The source’s shift discussion claims the two sides of (13) increase by C and 3C; substituting Y_1+C,Y_2+C instead leaves the contrast unchanged and adds 4C to the reward sum. These prose claims are not used to alter Theorem 2.

Condition 2 requires strict increase, positivity, reflected sum and limits, but does not require continuity or a derivative. Types A/B add differentiability away from zero. The theorem graphs keep these as separate requirements despite the source’s smoothed-loss terminology.

The final phrase says all t<t_0 without explicitly restricting t>0, although arbitrary positive real exponents are used. The intended small positive radius interpretation is recorded separately; the original t range is preserved. The exclusion of equality at the boundary permits atoms there.

The claimed equivalent contrast formulation drops absolute values and only controls positive small contrasts, whereas B controls both sides around one half. The saved theorem dependencies use B itself rather than this differing formula.

The condition literally bounds eta_1 and eta_2 away from zero. Decision boundaries occur at eta_t=1/2, so this does not imply the separation claimed in the surrounding prose and is not equivalent to an infinite noise exponent. Theorems 6/7 retain the literal source assumption without correction.

The later value display replaces fhat_t by phi(fhat_t) inside sign indicators. Under Condition 2 this always chooses positive actions, unlike the original value definition (5). The conflicting display is archived as A10; it is not substituted for the original definition.

Several sentences call V_psi(fhat) the psi-regret and V(fhat) the true regret, omitting the optimal-value subtraction. The original regret definitions and the actual theorem inequalities retain the subtraction. The informal wording does not redefine those quantities.

The informal class-approximation claim (20) omits scaling by a_n. Theorem 4 bounds scaled scores; Theorem 5 assumes explicitly that approximants in U_n divided by a_n are close to eta_t-1/2. No unstated scaling closure of U_n is added.

Theorem 5 does not explicitly impose the derivative-tail types A/B used in Theorem 4, while Condition 2 alone supplies no quantitative tail approach to its limits. The source scope is preserved with Condition 2 only; no proof-derived derivative condition is added to make the displayed rate easier to justify.

The source calls N the bracketing entropy but defines a number of brackets. Theorems 5/7 bound N, whereas (23) for Theorem 6 bounds log N with exponent 2rho_n. The metrics also differ; these conditions are not merged.

Bounds involving L2(P_n) depend on the observed sample. The main text does not state whether these inequalities are deterministic over all samples, almost sure, or on a specified event, nor an explicit epsilon range or uniformity of the implicit constants. These quantifier omissions are retained as unresolved.

The bracketing definition is for scalar functions, while (24) uses the pair class U_n with L2(P_n). The source does not specify a pair norm or identify the induced scalar loss class here. The formula is preserved without replacing U_n by its coordinate classes or a loss class.

Theorem 4 binds a_n tending to infinity but only calls delta_n a small number; it does not explicitly require delta_n to tend to zero. In Theorems 5-7 the probability guarantee is stated for each n,x, not as one event simultaneously covering all n,x. Uniformity of constants over varying rho_n, A_n and distributions is not fully specified.

ambient_resolution.shared: D1 fixes the two-stage observed record, histories, population law and empirical law, with potential-regime context. D2 gives propensities. Assumptions I,II,III,IV are separately D3,D4,D5,D7. D6 preserves the conditional treatment contrasts and continuation reward U_2*. D8 defines optimal regimes; D9 the real measurable score class; D10 the original score value; D11 the general surrogate value; D12 the maximizing-score/sign-rule correspondence; D13 the two regrets; D14 the eta maps and their one-half boundaries. Standard ambient objects include conditional expectation, probability, measurable functions, sign, finite-dimensional effective domains, upper semicontinuity, derivatives, suprema/infima, bracketing numbers, L2 norms, supremum norms, logarithms, limits and asymptotic comparisons. A1-A3 resolve source domains and notation. No supplement material was opened.
ambient_resolution.1: The conclusion negates the universal sequential Fisher-consistency predicate D16, which quantifies over laws satisfying I-IV and sequences in F. Closedness and strict concavity are D17,D18; boundedness above and smoothness are inline. A2 resolves the mixed derivative psi_12 and interior of the effective domain. Neither the product-surrogate family nor the later sample/entropy assumptions are prerequisites. The proof’s special deterministic second-stage construction is not imported.
ambient_resolution.2: The theorem explicitly assumes I-IV, fixes the hinge function D29 and requires both outcomes bounded below by a positive constant. D8 supplies d*, D12 supplies dtilde, and D20 gives the strict condition (13), including the definition of T(H_2,a_2). Both stage branches, set-valued outcomes, the equality to the first-stage rule and the source history ordering remain as printed. No uniqueness, Condition 2, small-noise condition or derivative type is added.
ambient_resolution.3: The assumptions are I-IV and the explicit Y_1,Y_2>0 condition. D19 supplies Condition 2, with C_phi, and the bivariate product is bound directly in the theorem. The two regrets are D13. The divisor (C_phi/2)^2 is retained exactly. The theorem gives a quantitative regret inequality; Fisher consistency follows in the next paragraph but that does not make the Fisher-consistency predicate a dependency needed to state this inequality.
ambient_resolution.4: The theorem assumes I-IV, outcome bound A (D24) and small-noise B (D25). A11 resolves alpha=min(alpha_1,alpha_2). D14 supplies eta_1,eta_2. D27/D28 supply the two derivative types, hence Condition 2; A7 supplies the product psi. The maps, a_n, delta_n, alpha-prime, kappa cases and exact rates are inline. The extra {0,1} domain factor is retained. No fitted empirical classifier, entropy restriction, optimization error, strong-separation condition or neural-network smoothness is needed.
ambient_resolution.5: The assumptions are I-IV, A, B and the later product-surrogate convention A7. D31 resolves (21), the coordinatewise sup-norm bracketing-number bound; its additional rho_n,A_n rates and the scaled approximation (22) are inline. D22 supplies the fitted pair’s class membership and D23 the empirical optimization error. D13 and A9 specify population surrogate regret of fitted scores. A8 supplies known propensities. Neither strong separation C nor the derivative types of Theorem 4 are silently added.
ambient_resolution.6: The assumptions are I-IV, A and the literal C (D26), with product surrogate A7 and known propensities A8. A12 supplies the logarithmic empirical-L2 bracketing condition (23), and D30 resolves its bracket count. The explicit rho_n range, A_n growth, approximation-error rate, positive k, Opt_n<1/2 and probability bound remain inline. D22/D23 supply class membership and optimization error. This theorem does not inherit B, (21), an exact empirical maximizer or any particular function-class implementation.
ambient_resolution.7: The assumptions are I-IV, A, literal C, the product-surrogate convention and known propensities. The bracketing-number inequality (24) is inline, with D30 defining N; it uses the pair class U_n in empirical L2 as printed. The approximation error (25), positive k, rho_n log A_n condition and final probability bound are inline. D22/D23 resolve fitted scores and optimization error. No Opt_n<1/2 condition or rho_n<1 condition is imported from Theorem 6. No neural-network, wavelet or Assumption D requirement is added.
